timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What exactly is entitlement management? Big words intimidate me.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: It's just organized access. Bundle permissions into access packages, put them in catalogs, control who gets them.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So it's like a shopping catalog for permissions?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Sort of! Users request an access package, it goes through approval, and they get exactly what they need.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: And access reviews are like an audit?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Periodic reviews where managers confirm people still need access. If not, it's revoked.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What about when someone leaves the company?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Lifecycle Workflows handle that automatically. Offboarding removes access, revokes sessions, cleans up.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Can it handle internal moves too? Like department transfers?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Yes! Attribute-based workflows trigger when department or role changes. Access adjusts automatically.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: How do you justify all this to management?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Business justification is part of the access request. Users explain why, creating an auditable trail.
